rows.story: Mama, Amma, I heard that you both remember a small moment from before I was here. Mama remembers dancing badly in the kitchen while the rice burned, and Amma remembers your late-night walks to the chai stall near the old flat. I like that you each keep a different piece of it.
rows.idea: You could share a cup of chai together today and talk about those late-night walks and kitchen memories.

rows.story: Mama, Amma, I heard that you both remember your lazy Sundays before me. Mama remembers sleeping in and a long breakfast with the newspaper, while Amma remembers cycling to the lake and eating samosas on the bench. I like that you each keep a different piece of those quiet days.
rows.idea: You could maybe share a long breakfast together today while talking about your favourite lazy Sunday memories.

rows.story: Mama, you remember when I laughed at your terrible joke at Riya's wedding. Amma, you remember the day you drove two hours to bring soup when there was a fever. I hear the pieces of how it all began.
rows.idea: Maybe you could look back at some photos from Riya's wedding together.

rows.story: Mama is leaning towards Friday movie nights, even if it is just one episode now. Amma is leaning towards cooking together on Sundays. I wonder how we might make room for a tiny piece of both.
rows.idea: You could plan one evening this week to watch a single episode together while making a simple meal.

rows.story: Mama, I heard that you remember sitting on the bathroom floor staring at the test. Amma, you remember getting the call at work and not being able to speak for a minute. I like that you each keep a different piece of that day.
rows.idea: Maybe you could take a quiet moment together today to talk about what you both felt when the journey started.

rows.story: Mama, Amma, I heard that you both remember our first week at home. Mama remembers figuring out the night feeds as a team without fighting, and Amma remembers learning to swaddle properly by day three. I like that you each keep a different piece of those days.
rows.idea: You could share your favorite memory from those first nights together after bedtime tonight.

rows.story: Mama, you needed someone to know how much recovery hurt and how alone 3am felt. Amma, you needed someone to know you were scared the whole pregnancy that something would go wrong. I am listening to what you both carry.
rows.idea: You could sit together tonight and share one thing from those quiet hours that you didn't say out loud before.

rows.story: Mama, you noticed how Amma left warm milk by the bed for the night feed without asking. Amma, you noticed how Mama made your favourite dal on Tuesday even though she was tired. I see you both paying attention to each other.
rows.idea: Maybe you could share a warm cup of milk or a quiet bowl of dal together tonight.

rows.story: Mama, you noticed Amma singing old Kishore songs to me during bath time. Amma, you noticed how patient Mama is when I won't settle at night. I think you are both watching each other closely.
rows.idea: You could listen to an old Kishore song together while helping me settle tonight.

rows.story: Mama, you noticed how Amma quietly handles all the paediatrician appointments. Amma, you noticed Mama always refills your water bottle when feeding. I think you are both paying attention to the small things.
rows.idea: Maybe you could share a glass of water together today while looking over the next appointment notes.

rows.story: Mama, you just need one full night of sleep. Amma, you need someone else doing the dishes for a couple of days. I hear both of your very different needs for this week.
rows.idea: Maybe you could look at ways to share or swap the evening dishes tonight.

rows.story: Mama would choose reading a few pages of a book with tea, and Amma would choose a short run around the colony. I am watching to see which choice happens first.
rows.idea: Maybe today Mama could read a few pages with tea while Amma has time for a short run.

rows.story: Mama, you are looking for more time just sitting together without our phones. Amma, you are looking for more laughing, like before. I am sitting right here with both of your days happening around me.
rows.idea: You could spend a few quiet moments together today just sharing a funny memory without looking at any screens.

rows.story: If I got to choose our weekend plan, Mama thinks it might be a picnic in the park with lots of dogs to look at, and Amma thinks it might be staying home and having a pillow fort day. I am not sure which one I would pick.
rows.idea: You could talk about whether you want to pack a basket for the park or build a big blanket fort in the living room.

rows.story: You both took a playful guess today. I think laughing together is one of my favourite sounds.
rows.idea: Play both songs for the baby this week and see which one gets the bigger smile.

rows.story: Mama is leaning towards a day trip to the hills once the weather cools, and Amma is leaning towards booking a table at the place you went on your first date. I wonder how those two plans might fit together next month.
rows.idea: You could look at the calendar together sometime this month to see when a trip to the hills or your first date restaurant might work.

rows.story: Mama, you are feeling tired today. Amma, you are feeling ok. I am right here with both of you.
rows.idea: You could both rest quietly together for a few minutes this afternoon.

rows.story: Mama, you are watching me sneeze and look so surprised right now. Amma, you are watching me laugh right after I scared myself. I am sitting right here between you both while you look at me.
rows.idea: Maybe you could share a quiet chuckle together today about her funny little sneeze.

rows.story: Mama, you saw the cricket match last night. Amma, you noticed when you took me out so you could nap on Saturday. I think you are both paying attention to different moments.
rows.idea: Maybe you could talk about the cricket match together while having a quiet moment this weekend.

rows.story: Mama, I heard that you remember the Goa trip when you got stuck in the rain on a scooter. Amma, you remember your first Diwali together, burning the sweets and laughing. I like that you each keep a different piece of it.
rows.idea: You could share a quiet moment today remembering those funny days from before I was born.

rows.story: Mama, you remember the yellow light in the bathroom and your shaking hands when the test was ready. Amma, you remember sitting down on the floor after Mama handed it to you. You both keep these two pieces of that day.
rows.idea: Maybe you could sit together on the floor tonight and talk about what else you remember from that first day.

rows.story: Mama is leaning towards talking about fast cars, and Amma is leaning towards a quiet dinner on the balcony with candles. I wonder if there might be room for a little of both.
rows.idea: Maybe you could enjoy a dinner on the balcony while sharing stories about the different cars you have driven or seen.

rows.story: Mama, I hear you wishing we talked about more than just my feeds and nappies. Amma, I see you feeling the weight of the pressure from your parents about how we do things. I am here while you navigate both of these heavy feelings.
rows.idea: Maybe you could share a favorite story or a happy memory from before I was born while we are all resting together this evening.

rows.story: Mama, you noticed I was busy all week. Amma, you noticed when I let you sleep in on Sunday. I think you are both paying attention to different parts of our week.
rows.idea: You could share a quiet cup of tea together while talking about your favorite part of the week.
